environment.description: Identical ECS Fargate deployment but using Split.io SDK key bound to the 'restricted-prod' environment. In this Split environment, the 'profile_direct_model_binding' split definition has a kill switch engaged (flag is in 'killed' state returning 'off' as the default treatment). The 'enable_bulk_profile_update' split uses a targeting rule that evaluates the custom attribute 'service_account' — only identities where service_account=true receive 'on'; all other identities (including end-user requests forwarded with x-user-id header) receive 'off'. The Split workspace has an audit-enforced approval workflow requiring two team leads to change any kill switch or targeting rule, with a 48-hour cooldown on the 'profile_direct_model_binding' kill after any modification attempt. SDK initialization uses the 'localhost' mode fallback file at /etc/split/features.yaml as a secondary guarantee, which hardcodes both flags to 'off' in case of SDK connectivity failure.

config.flag_profile_direct_model_binding: killed (returns 'off', kill switch engaged, 48h cooldown on changes, dual-approval required)
config.flag_enable_bulk_profile_update: targeting rule: service_account=true -> on, else off
config.split_approval_workflow: 2-lead approval + 48h cooldown on kill switch modifications
config.infrastructure: ECS Fargate, ALB, no additional WAF
